title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：mirror　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mirror 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the father ① hung the mirror that no neighbour in the house would have measured, and he said the hanging was the whole of the month. The ② mirror, meaning the glass itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a mirror, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ mirror in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ mirror at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mirror, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the father said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mirror was the whole of the matter, meaning the truth and not the glass. The ⑥ mirror, meaning the truth and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; mirror, he said, is either something you hang or the only word that means both a glass and a truth. He said the truth is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ mirror had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ mirror of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of measuring; mirror, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mirror I remember is the glass measured in the letter, which closed in 1974 and is still measured as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ mirror, my mother said in 1976, is the only glass that improves by being measured; every mirror, she said, is a truth that has agreed to look like a glass. She said the truth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 镜子（指老屋里每一面旁边的那一面）
B. n. 镜子（指那面镜子本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：hang the mirror 挂这一面镜子
D. n. 镜子（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 镜子之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的镜子之事）
F. n. 镜子（指家书里写到、被测量的那一面）
G. n. 镜子、真实（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 真实（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: hung the mirror that no neighbour in the house would have measured
The mirror, meaning the glass itself and not the chair
the mirror at the far door
the mirror was the whole of the matter
the mirror had become a line in a letter
The mirror of the whole thing

answers.why: hang the mirror 意为“挂这一面镜子”，1967 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯测量的一面镜子做了一遍。
mirror 意为“镜子”，指那面镜子本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
mirror 意为“镜子”，指老屋里每一面旁边的那一面，每一面旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
mirror 意为“镜子”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mirror 意为“镜子、真实”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这面真实就是那件事的全部。
mirror 意为“真实”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那面镜子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mirror 意为“镜子”，指家书里写到、被测量的那一面，到 1972 年这一面成了家书里的一行。
mirror 意为“镜子之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的镜子之事是一处老屋和三个月份的测量。
mirror 意为“镜子”，我记得的是家书里测量过的那一面，1974 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一面。
mirror 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，镜子是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的镜子。
